question: What did God create in the beginning?
verse: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.
explanation: The very first verse of the Bible tells us that God is the Creator of everything that exists.

question: What did God tell Noah to build?
verse: Make yourself an ark of gopherwood; make rooms in the ark, and cover it inside and outside with pitch.
explanation: God warned Noah about the coming flood and told him to build a huge boat to save his family and the animals.

question: What sign did God put in the clouds after the flood?
verse: I set My rainbow in the cloud, and it shall be for the sign of the covenant between Me and the earth.
explanation: The rainbow is God's promise that He will never again destroy the whole earth with a flood.

question: What did David use to defeat Goliath?
verse: Then David put his hand in his bag and took out a stone; and he slung it and struck the Philistine in his forehead, so that the stone sank into his forehead, and he fell on his face to the earth.
explanation: Young David trusted God instead of armor, and God gave him victory over the giant.

question: What swallowed Jonah?
verse: Now the LORD had prepared a great fish to swallow Jonah. And Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.
explanation: Jonah ran from God's call to preach in Nineveh, but God used a great fish to bring him back.

question: Finish the verse: "The LORD is my ___; I shall not want."
verse: The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.
explanation: David, who was once a shepherd himself, describes how God guides, protects and provides for His people.

question: What animals did God keep from hurting Daniel?
verse: My God sent His angel and shut the lions' mouths, so that they have not hurt me, because I was found innocent before Him; and also, O king, I have done no wrong before you.
explanation: Daniel kept praying to God even when it was against the law, and God protected him in the lions' den.

question: What did God form the first man from?
verse: And the LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living being.
explanation: God personally made Adam and gave him life with His own breath.

question: Which sea did God part so Israel could cross on dry land?
verse: Then Moses stretched out his hand over the sea; and the LORD caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind all that night, and made the sea into dry land, and the waters were divided.
explanation: God rescued Israel from Pharaoh's army by opening a path through the sea.

question: How many commandments did God write on the stone tablets?
verse: So he was there with the LORD forty days and forty nights; he neither ate bread nor drank water. And He wrote on the tablets the words of the covenant, the Ten Commandments.
explanation: On Mount Sinai God gave Moses the Ten Commandments to show His people how to love Him and each other.

question: On which day did God rest from His work of creation?
verse: And on the seventh day God ended His work which He had done, and He rested on the seventh day from all His work which He had done.
explanation: God finished creation in six days and rested on the seventh, giving us a pattern of work and rest.

question: What was the name of the son born to Abraham and Sarah in their old age?
verse: And Abraham called the name of his son who was born to him—whom Sarah bore to him—Isaac.
explanation: God kept His promise to give Abraham and Sarah a son, even though they were very old.

question: What special gift did Jacob (Israel) give his son Joseph?
verse: Now Israel loved Joseph more than all his children, because he was the son of his old age. Also he made him a tunic of many colors.
explanation: The colorful tunic showed Jacob's favor toward Joseph, which made his brothers jealous.

question: What happened to the walls of Jericho when the people shouted?
verse: So the people shouted when the priests blew the trumpets. And it happened when the people heard the sound of the trumpet, and the people shouted with a great shout, that the wall fell down flat. Then the people went up into the city, every man straight before him, and they took the city.
explanation: Israel obeyed God's unusual battle plan, and God brought the walls down.

question: What would happen to Samson's strength if his head was shaved?
choices: It would move to his arms
verse: that he told her all his heart, and said to her, "No razor has ever come upon my head, for I have been a Nazirite to God from my mother's womb. If I am shaven, then my strength will leave me, and I shall become weak, and be like any other man."
explanation: Samson's uncut hair was a sign of his Nazirite vow to God, the true source of his strength.

question: Who did God say would speak for Moses because he could speak well?
verse: So the anger of the LORD was kindled against Moses, and He said: "Is not Aaron the Levite your brother? I know that he can speak well. And look, he is also coming out to meet you. When he sees you, he will be glad in his heart."
explanation: Moses felt unable to speak to Pharaoh, so God gave him his brother Aaron as a helper.

question: Who said, "Your people shall be my people, and your God, my God"?
verse: But Ruth said: "Entreat me not to leave you, Or to turn back from following after you; For wherever you go, I will go; And wherever you lodge, I will lodge; Your people shall be my people, And your God, my God."
explanation: Ruth stayed loyal to her mother-in-law Naomi and chose to follow the God of Israel.

question: What was unusual about the burning bush Moses saw?
choices: It was not consumed by the fire
verse: And the Angel of the LORD appeared to him in a flame of fire from the midst of a bush. So he looked, and behold, the bush was burning with fire, but the bush was not consumed.
explanation: God got Moses' attention with this miracle and then called him to lead Israel out of Egypt.

question: What did King Solomon ask God for?
choices: An understanding heart to judge the people
verse: Therefore give to Your servant an understanding heart to judge Your people, that I may discern between good and evil. For who is able to judge this great people of Yours?
explanation: God was pleased that Solomon asked for wisdom, and gave him riches and honor as well.

question: How was Elijah taken up into heaven?
choices: By a whirlwind, with a chariot of fire
On the back of an eagle
In a cloud on a mountain
verse: Then it happened, as they continued on and talked, that suddenly a chariot of fire appeared with horses of fire, and separated the two of them; and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven.
explanation: Elijah did not die but was taken to heaven while his helper Elisha watched.

question: How many men did King Nebuchadnezzar see walking in the fiery furnace?
verse: "Look!" he answered, "I see four men loose, walking in the midst of the fire; and they are not hurt, and the form of the fourth is like the Son of God."
explanation: Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-Nego refused to bow to an idol, and God was with them in the fire.

question: Finish the verse: "Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and lean not on your own ___."
verse: Trust in the LORD with all your heart, And lean not on your own understanding;
explanation: This proverb teaches us to depend on God's wisdom more than our own.

question: Who was told she may have come to the kingdom "for such a time as this"?
verse: For if you remain completely silent at this time, relief and deliverance will arise for the Jews from another place, but you and your father's house will perish. Yet who knows whether you have come to the kingdom for such a time as this?
explanation: Mordecai encouraged Queen Esther to bravely speak to the king to save her people.

question: What new name did God give Jacob?
verse: And He said, "Your name shall no longer be called Jacob, but Israel; for you have struggled with God and with men, and have prevailed."
explanation: After wrestling all night, Jacob received a new name, which became the name of the whole nation.

question: What did the Israelites call the bread God sent from heaven in the wilderness?
verse: And the house of Israel called its name Manna. And it was like white coriander seed, and the taste of it was like wafers made with honey.
explanation: God fed His people every day for forty years in the desert.

question: In Isaiah 53:6, what animal are we compared to for going astray?
verse: All we like sheep have gone astray; We have turned, every one, to his own way; And the LORD has laid on Him the iniquity of us all.
explanation: Isaiah foretold that God would place our sins on His Servant, fulfilled in Jesus.

question: What did Gideon put on the threshing floor to test God's promise?
verse: look, I shall put a fleece of wool on the threshing floor; if there is dew on the fleece only, and it is dry on all the ground, then I shall know that You will save Israel by my hand, as You have said.
explanation: God patiently answered Gideon's request and gave him confidence to lead Israel.

question: What did young Samuel answer when God called him?
verse: Now the LORD came and stood and called as at other times, "Samuel! Samuel!" And Samuel answered, "Speak, for Your servant hears."
explanation: Samuel learned to recognize God's voice and grew up to be a great prophet.

question: Finish the verse: "Be strong and of good courage; do not be afraid... for the LORD your God is with you ___."
verse: Have I not commanded you? Be strong and of good courage; do not be afraid, nor be dismayed, for the LORD your God is with you wherever you go.
explanation: God encouraged Joshua as he took over leading Israel after Moses.

question: What did Hannah name the son God gave her after she prayed?
verse: So it came to pass in the process of time that Hannah conceived and bore a son, and called his name Samuel, saying, "Because I have asked for him from the LORD."
explanation: Hannah prayed for a child, and God answered. She dedicated Samuel to serve the Lord.

question: According to Micah 6:8, what does the LORD require?
choices: To do justly, love mercy, and walk humbly with God
verse: He has shown you, O man, what is good; And what does the LORD require of you But to do justly, To love mercy, And to walk humbly with your God?
explanation: God cares more about a faithful heart and how we treat others than about outward rituals.

question: Which town did Micah prophesy would be the birthplace of Israel's Ruler?
verse: But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, Though you are little among the thousands of Judah, Yet out of you shall come forth to Me The One to be Ruler in Israel, Whose goings forth are from of old, From everlasting.
explanation: Hundreds of years before Jesus was born, Micah named the small town where He would be born.

question: How old was Methuselah when he died?
verse: So all the days of Methuselah were nine hundred and sixty-nine years; and he died.
explanation: Methuselah is the oldest person recorded in the Bible.

question: Which man "walked with God; and he was not, for God took him"?
verse: And Enoch walked with God; and he was not, for God took him.
explanation: Enoch had such a close relationship with God that God took him without his dying.

question: How many days did it take to rebuild Jerusalem's wall under Nehemiah?
verse: So the wall was finished on the twenty-fifth day of Elul, in fifty-two days.
explanation: Despite opposition, the people worked together and God helped them finish quickly.

question: In Isaiah 7:14, what name would the virgin's Son be called?
verse: Therefore the Lord Himself will give you a sign: Behold, the virgin shall conceive and bear a Son, and shall call His name Immanuel.
explanation: Immanuel means "God with us," and Matthew tells us this was fulfilled in Jesus.

question: Whose donkey spoke to him?
verse: Then the LORD opened the mouth of the donkey, and she said to Balaam, "What have I done to you, that you have struck me these three times?"
explanation: God used a talking donkey to stop Balaam, who was heading off to curse Israel.

question: Which prophet wrote, "For I know the thoughts that I think toward you... to give you a future and a hope"?
verse: For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, says the LORD, thoughts of peace and not of evil, to give you a future and a hope.
explanation: Jeremiah wrote this to Israelites in exile in Babylon, reminding them God had good plans for them.

question: Which prophet wrote, "the just shall live by his faith"?
verse: Behold the proud, His soul is not upright in him; But the just shall live by his faith.
explanation: This verse is quoted three times in the New Testament to explain that we are saved through faith.

question: What happened to Lot's wife when she looked back at Sodom?
choices: She became a pillar of salt
She was carried off by angels
verse: But his wife looked back behind him, and she became a pillar of salt.
explanation: The angels told Lot's family not to look back, and her disobedience cost her life.

question: Which prophet was told to preach to a valley of dry bones?
verse: Again He said to me, "Prophesy to these bones, and say to them, 'O dry bones, hear the word of the LORD!'"
explanation: The bones coming to life pictured God restoring the nation of Israel.

question: How old was Josiah when he became king?
verse: Josiah was eight years old when he became king, and he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jedidah the daughter of Adaiah of Bozkath.
explanation: Josiah became one of Judah's most faithful kings, leading the people back to God's law.

question: Who was king of Salem and priest of God Most High in Abraham's day?
verse: Then Melchizedek king of Salem brought out bread and wine; he was the priest of God Most High.
explanation: The book of Hebrews compares Jesus to Melchizedek as our eternal priest.

question: Whom did God tell the prophet Hosea to marry?
verse: So he went and took Gomer the daughter of Diblaim, and she conceived and bore him a son.
explanation: Hosea's marriage to an unfaithful wife pictured God's faithful love for unfaithful Israel.

question: Which book contains "Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God, the LORD is one!"?
verse: Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God, the LORD is one!
explanation: Called the Shema, this is one of the most important statements of faith in Israel; Jesus quoted it as part of the greatest commandment.

question: According to John 3:16, why did God give His only begotten Son?
choices: Because He so loved the world
verse: For God so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son, that whoever believes in Him should not perish but have everlasting life.
explanation: This verse sums up the gospel: God's love moved Him to send Jesus so that everyone who believes can have eternal life.

question: In what town was Jesus born?
verse: Now after Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea in the days of Herod the king, behold, wise men from the East came to Jerusalem,
explanation: Jesus was born in Bethlehem, the town of King David, just as the prophet Micah had foretold.

question: What name did the angel tell Mary to give her Son?
verse: And behold, you will conceive in your womb and bring forth a Son, and shall call His name JESUS.
explanation: The name Jesus means "the LORD saves."

question: Where did Mary lay baby Jesus?
verse: And she brought forth her firstborn Son, and wrapped Him in swaddling cloths, and laid Him in a manger, because there was no room for them in the inn.
explanation: The Son of God was born in a humble place, with an animal feeding trough for a bed.

question: How many disciples did Jesus choose?
verse: And when He had called His twelve disciples to Him, He gave them power over unclean spirits, to cast them out, and to heal all kinds of sickness and all kinds of disease.
explanation: Jesus chose twelve men to follow Him, learn from Him, and carry on His work.

question: What food did the disciples have before Jesus fed the 5,000?
verse: And they said to Him, "We have here only five loaves and two fish."
explanation: Jesus blessed this small meal and fed thousands, with twelve baskets left over.

question: How did Jesus go out to the disciples' boat in the storm?
verse: Now in the fourth watch of the night Jesus went to them, walking on the sea.
explanation: Jesus showed His power over nature and told His frightened disciples, "Be of good cheer! It is I."

question: Who baptized Jesus in the Jordan River?
verse: Then Jesus came from Galilee to John at the Jordan to be baptized by him.
explanation: When Jesus was baptized, the Spirit came down like a dove and the Father spoke from heaven.

question: What did the angel tell the women at Jesus' empty tomb?
choices: "He is not here; for He is risen"
"He has gone to Galilee to hide"
verse: He is not here; for He is risen, as He said. Come, see the place where the Lord lay.
explanation: Jesus rose from the dead on the third day, just as He had promised.

question: What did Jesus turn water into at the wedding in Cana?
verse: When the master of the feast had tasted the water that was made wine, and did not know where it came from (but the servants who had drawn the water knew), the master of the feast called the bridegroom.
explanation: This was the first of Jesus' miraculous signs, showing His glory to His disciples.

question: What did Zacchaeus climb so he could see Jesus?
verse: So he ran ahead and climbed up into a sycamore tree to see Him, for He was going to pass that way.
explanation: Zacchaeus was short, but Jesus noticed him, went to his house, and changed his life.

question: How many times did Jesus say Peter would deny Him before the rooster crowed?
verse: And Peter remembered the word of Jesus who had said to him, "Before the rooster crows, you will deny Me three times." So he went out and wept bitterly.
explanation: Peter failed, but after the resurrection Jesus lovingly restored him.

question: Finish the Golden Rule: "Whatever you want men to do to you, ___."
verse: Therefore, whatever you want men to do to you, do also to them, for this is the Law and the Prophets.
explanation: Jesus taught that we should treat others the way we want to be treated.

question: How does the Lord's Prayer begin?
verse: In this manner, therefore, pray: Our Father in heaven, Hallowed be Your name.
explanation: Jesus taught His disciples to pray to God as their loving Father.

question: What did Jesus say when the disciples tried to keep children away?
choices: "Let the little children come to Me"
verse: But when Jesus saw it, He was greatly displeased and said to them, "Let the little children come to Me, and do not forbid them; for of such is the kingdom of God."
explanation: Jesus welcomed children and said we must receive God's kingdom with childlike trust.

question: Which angel was sent to Mary in Nazareth?
verse: Now in the sixth month the angel Gabriel was sent by God to a city of Galilee named Nazareth,
explanation: Gabriel announced that Mary would be the mother of Jesus. He had also visited Zacharias about John's birth.

question: Where was Saul going when a light from heaven shone around him?
verse: As he journeyed he came near Damascus, and suddenly a light shone around him from heaven.
explanation: Saul was on his way to arrest Christians when Jesus met him. He became the apostle Paul.

question: Which is the first fruit of the Spirit listed in Galatians 5:22?
verse: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control. Against such there is no law.
explanation: These qualities grow in our lives as the Holy Spirit works in us.

question: Whom did Jesus call out of the tomb, alive again?
verse: Now when He had said these things, He cried with a loud voice, "Lazarus, come forth!"
explanation: Lazarus had been dead four days, and Jesus raised him to show He is the resurrection and the life.

question: In Jesus' parable, who stopped to help the hurt traveler?
verse: But a certain Samaritan, as he journeyed, came where he was. And when he saw him, he had compassion.
explanation: Jesus used the Good Samaritan to teach that our neighbor is anyone who needs our help.

question: How much was Judas paid to betray Jesus?
verse: and said, "What are you willing to give me if I deliver Him to you?" And they counted out to him thirty pieces of silver.
explanation: This fulfilled a prophecy in Zechariah about the price paid for the Shepherd.

question: What happened when the disciples were filled with the Holy Spirit at Pentecost?
verse: And they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance.
explanation: People from many nations heard the gospel in their own languages, and about 3,000 believed that day.

question: Finish Jesus' words: "I am the way, the truth, and the ___."
verse: Jesus said to him, "I am the way, the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through Me."
explanation: Jesus said this to comfort His disciples: He is the only way to the Father.

question: In the parable of the prodigal son, what did the father do when he saw his son coming home?
choices: Sent a servant to scold him
Made him work in the fields first
verse: And he arose and came to his father. But when he was still a great way off, his father saw him and had compassion, and ran and fell on his neck and kissed him.
explanation: The father's welcome shows how God joyfully forgives those who come back to Him.

question: According to Romans 3:23, who has sinned?
verse: for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God,
explanation: Everyone needs God's grace, which is why we all need Jesus.

question: What was Matthew's job when Jesus called him?
verse: As Jesus passed on from there, He saw a man named Matthew sitting at the tax office. And He said to him, "Follow Me." So he arose and followed Him.
explanation: Tax collectors were disliked, but Jesus called Matthew, who later wrote the Gospel of Matthew.

question: Which disciple was invited to touch Jesus' hands and side?
verse: Then He said to Thomas, "Reach your finger here, and look at My hands; and reach your hand here, and put it into My side. Do not be unbelieving, but believing."
explanation: Thomas doubted the resurrection until he saw Jesus, then said, "My Lord and my God!"

question: According to 1 Corinthians 13:13, which is the greatest: faith, hope, or love?
verse: And now abide faith, hope, love, these three; but the greatest of these is love.
explanation: Paul's "love chapter" teaches that love is the most important gift of all.

question: Finish the verse: "I can do all things through Christ who ___."
verse: I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me.
explanation: Paul wrote this from prison, saying Christ gave him strength in every situation, good or hard.

question: In the Great Commission, what did Jesus tell His disciples to do?
choices: Make disciples of all the nations
Wait in the upper room forever
verse: Go therefore and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,
explanation: Before returning to heaven, Jesus sent His followers to share the gospel with the whole world.

question: What is the shortest verse in the English Bible?
verse: Jesus wept.
explanation: Even knowing He would raise Lazarus, Jesus shared the grief of His friends.

question: Which book says, "Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen"?
verse: Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.
explanation: Hebrews 11 goes on to list many Old Testament heroes who lived by faith.

question: What were Paul and Silas doing in prison at midnight?
verse: But at midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, and the prisoners were listening to them.
explanation: An earthquake opened the prison, and the jailer and his family came to believe in Jesus.

question: Who was the first Christian martyr, stoned while praying?
verse: And they stoned Stephen as he was calling on God and saying, "Lord Jesus, receive my spirit."
explanation: Stephen forgave his attackers. Saul, the future apostle Paul, stood watching.

question: Which young man fell asleep and fell from a window during Paul's long sermon?
verse: And in a window sat a certain young man named Eutychus, who was sinking into a deep sleep. He was overcome by sleep; and as Paul continued speaking, he fell down from the third story and was taken up dead.
explanation: Paul went down, embraced him, and God brought Eutychus back to life.

question: According to Ephesians 2:8, how are we saved?
choices: By being born into a good family
verse: For by grace you have been saved through faith, and that not of yourselves; it is the gift of God,
explanation: Salvation is a free gift from God, not something we earn.

question: In Revelation, Jesus says He is the Alpha and the Omega. What does that mean?
verse: I am the Alpha and the Omega, the Beginning and the End, the First and the Last.
explanation: Alpha and Omega are the first and last letters of the Greek alphabet.

question: On what island was John when he received the Revelation?
verse: I, John, both your brother and companion in the tribulation and kingdom and patience of Jesus Christ, was on the island that is called Patmos for the word of God and for the testimony of Jesus Christ.
explanation: John had been exiled to Patmos for preaching about Jesus.

question: Who asked Jesus, "How can a man be born when he is old?"
verse: Nicodemus said to Him, "How can a man be born when he is old? Can he enter a second time into his mother's womb and be born?"
explanation: Jesus explained to this Pharisee that being "born again" is a spiritual new birth from God.

question: Which apostle's name means "Son of Encouragement"?
verse: And Joses, who was also named Barnabas by the apostles (which is translated Son of Encouragement), a Levite of the country of Cyprus,
explanation: Barnabas lived up to his name, welcoming the new believer Paul and later traveling with him.

question: What did Lydia of Thyatira sell?
verse: Now a certain woman named Lydia heard us. She was a seller of purple from the city of Thyatira, who worshiped God. The Lord opened her heart to heed the things spoken by Paul.
explanation: Lydia was one of the first believers in Europe and opened her home to Paul and his friends.

question: According to Romans 8:28, what works together for good to those who love God?
verse: And we know that all things work together for good to those who love God, to those who are the called according to His purpose.
explanation: God can use every circumstance, even hard ones, for the good of His people.

question: Which prophet was the Ethiopian official reading when Philip met him?
verse: So Philip ran to him, and heard him reading the prophet Isaiah, and said, "Do you understand what you are reading?"
explanation: Philip explained that Isaiah was speaking about Jesus, and the official was baptized.

question: Who was chosen to replace Judas as one of the twelve apostles?
verse: And they cast their lots, and the lot fell on Matthias. And he was numbered with the eleven apostles.
explanation: The apostles prayed and chose Matthias, who had followed Jesus since His baptism.

question: According to 2 Timothy 3:16, how is all Scripture given?
verse: All Scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness,
explanation: The Bible is God-breathed and useful for teaching us how to live.

question: How many years did God add to King Hezekiah's life?
verse: Go and tell Hezekiah, 'Thus says the LORD, the God of David your father: "I have heard your prayer, I have seen your tears; surely I will add to your days fifteen years."'
explanation: Hezekiah was deathly ill, but God answered his tearful prayer and gave him fifteen more years.

question: Which judge of Israel is described as left-handed?
verse: But when the children of Israel cried out to the LORD, the LORD raised up a deliverer for them: Ehud the son of Gera, the Benjamite, a left-handed man. By him the children of Israel sent tribute to Eglon king of Moab.
explanation: God used Ehud's left-handedness to free Israel from Eglon, king of Moab.

question: What did Shamgar use to strike down six hundred Philistines?
verse: After him was Shamgar the son of Anath, who killed six hundred men of the Philistines with an ox goad; and he also delivered Israel.
explanation: Shamgar gets only one verse in the Bible, but God used a simple farm tool to deliver Israel through him.

question: What was the bed of Og, king of Bashan, made of?
verse: For only Og king of Bashan remained of the remnant of the giants. Indeed his bedstead was an iron bedstead. (Is it not in Rabbah of the people of Ammon?) Nine cubits is its length and four cubits its width, according to the standard cubit.
explanation: Og was one of the last giants, and his iron bed was about 13 feet long. God still gave Israel victory over him.

question: What was the name of Jonathan's son who was lame in his feet?
verse: Jonathan, Saul's son, had a son who was lame in his feet. He was five years old when the news about Saul and Jonathan came from Jezreel; and his nurse took him up and fled. And it happened, as she made haste to flee, that he fell and became lame. His name was Mephibosheth.
explanation: Later King David showed kindness to Mephibosheth for Jonathan's sake and let him eat at the king's table.

question: Who defeated the Canaanite commander Sisera with a tent peg?
verse: Then Jael, Heber's wife, took a tent peg and took a hammer in her hand, and went softly to him and drove the peg into his temple, and it went down into the ground; for he was fast asleep and weary. So he died.
explanation: Deborah had foretold that the victory over Sisera would go to a woman, and it happened through Jael.

question: Whom did God fill with His Spirit to craft the furnishings of the tabernacle?
verse: See, I have called by name Bezalel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah. And I have filled him with the Spirit of God, in wisdom, in understanding, in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship,
explanation: Bezalel is the first person the Bible says was filled with the Spirit of God, and it was for artistic skill.

question: What did Elisha make float after it fell into the Jordan River?
verse: So the man of God said, "Where did it fall?" And he showed him the place. So he cut off a stick, and threw it in there; and he made the iron float.
explanation: The axe head was borrowed, and God cared about this small problem for one of the prophets.

question: How many men did God use with Gideon to defeat the Midianites?
verse: Then the LORD said to Gideon, "By the three hundred men who lapped I will save you, and deliver the Midianites into your hand. Let all the other people go, every man to his place."
explanation: God cut Gideon's army from 32,000 to 300 so Israel would know the victory came from Him.

question: Who was Moses' father-in-law, the priest of Midian?
verse: And Jethro, the priest of Midian, Moses' father-in-law, heard of all that God had done for Moses and for Israel His people—that the LORD had brought Israel out of Egypt.
explanation: Jethro later gave Moses wise advice to share the work of judging the people with other leaders.

question: What words did the hand write on the wall at King Belshazzar's feast?
verse: And this is the inscription that was written: MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN.
explanation: Daniel explained that God had weighed Belshazzar's kingdom and found it wanting. Babylon fell that very night.

question: Ruth's son Obed was the grandfather of which famous king?
verse: Also the neighbor women gave him a name, saying, "There is a son born to Naomi." And they called his name Obed. He is the father of Jesse, the father of David.
explanation: Ruth, a woman from Moab, became great-grandmother of King David and part of the family line of Jesus.

question: From what city did Terah and Abram set out toward Canaan?
verse: And Terah took his son Abram and his grandson Lot, the son of Haran, and his daughter-in-law Sarai, his son Abram's wife, and they went out with them from Ur of the Chaldeans to go to the land of Canaan; and they came to Haran and dwelt there.
explanation: Abram's family left Ur and stopped in Haran, where God later called Abram to go on to Canaan.

question: How was David's son Absalom caught during the battle?
choices: His head caught in a terebinth tree
He was trapped in a cave
verse: Then Absalom met the servants of David. Absalom rode on a mule. The mule went under the thick boughs of a great terebinth tree, and his head caught in the terebinth; so he was left hanging between heaven and earth. And the mule which was under him went on.
explanation: Absalom had rebelled against his father David. Even so, David grieved deeply when he died.

question: What birds brought food to Elijah by the Brook Cherith?
verse: The ravens brought him bread and meat in the morning, and bread and meat in the evening; and he drank from the brook.
explanation: During a drought, God provided for Elijah in a surprising way, through birds that usually take food rather than give it.

question: How many large fish were in the net in John 21?
verse: Simon Peter went up and dragged the net to land, full of large fish, one hundred and fifty-three; and although there were so many, the net was not broken.
explanation: After the resurrection, Jesus filled the disciples' empty net, then served them breakfast on the shore.

question: What was the name of the high priest's servant whose ear Peter cut off?
verse: Then Simon Peter, having a sword, drew it and struck the high priest's servant, and cut off his right ear. The servant's name was Malchus.
explanation: Luke tells us Jesus touched the servant's ear and healed him, even as He was being arrested.

question: Who had been promised by the Holy Spirit that he would see the Christ before he died?
verse: And behold, there was a man in Jerusalem whose name was Simeon, and this man was just and devout, waiting for the Consolation of Israel, and the Holy Spirit was upon him.
explanation: Simeon held baby Jesus in the temple and praised God that he had seen His salvation.

question: What was the Greek name of Tabitha, whom Peter raised in Joppa?
verse: At Joppa there was a certain disciple named Tabitha, which is translated Dorcas. This woman was full of good works and charitable deeds which she did.
explanation: Tabitha was known for making clothes for widows. God raised her to life through Peter, and many believed.

question: On which island was Paul shipwrecked on his way to Rome?
verse: Now when they had escaped, they then found out that the island was called Malta.
explanation: On Malta a viper bit Paul without harming him, and he healed many of the island's sick.

question: What trade did Paul share with Aquila and Priscilla?
verse: So, because he was of the same trade, he stayed with them and worked; for by occupation they were tentmakers.
explanation: Paul often worked with his hands to support himself so he would not be a burden while preaching.

question: What was the name of the girl who answered the door when Peter escaped prison?
verse: And as Peter knocked at the door of the gate, a girl named Rhoda came to answer.
explanation: Rhoda was so excited to hear Peter's voice that she ran to tell everyone and left him knocking outside.

question: About how old was Jesus when He began His ministry?
verse: Now Jesus Himself began His ministry at about thirty years of age, being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph, the son of Heli,
explanation: Luke gives Jesus' age right before listing His family line back to Adam.

question: For which runaway servant did Paul write to Philemon?
verse: I appeal to you for my son Onesimus, whom I have begotten while in my chains,
explanation: Onesimus became a Christian through Paul, who asked Philemon to welcome him back as a brother.

question: What was the name of Timothy's grandmother?
verse: when I call to remembrance the genuine faith that is in you, which dwelt first in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice, and I am persuaded is in you also.
explanation: Timothy's faith was passed down through his grandmother and mother, a picture of faith shared in families.

question: Which church in Revelation was called lukewarm?
verse: So then, because you are lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot, I will vomit you out of My mouth.
explanation: Laodicea was a wealthy city whose church had become spiritually comfortable and complacent.

question: When Mary and Joseph found 12-year-old Jesus in the temple, what did He say He must be about?
verse: And He said to them, "Why did you seek Me? Did you not know that I must be about My Father's business?"
explanation: These are the first recorded words of Jesus, and they show He knew God was His Father.

question: Where was Apollos, the eloquent teacher, born?
verse: Now a certain Jew named Apollos, born at Alexandria, an eloquent man and mighty in the Scriptures, came to Ephesus.
explanation: Priscilla and Aquila took Apollos aside and explained the way of God more accurately to him.

question: From which tribe of Israel did Paul come?
verse: circumcised the eighth day, of the stock of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of the Hebrews; concerning the law, a Pharisee;
explanation: Paul listed his impressive background, then said he counted it all as loss compared to knowing Christ.

question: In his letter, Jude calls himself the brother of whom?
verse: Jude, a bondservant of Jesus Christ, and brother of James, To those who are called, sanctified by God the Father, and preserved in Jesus Christ:
explanation: Jude and James are generally understood to be half-brothers of Jesus, yet Jude humbly calls himself a servant.
